strengths: Locals would recognize omiyage as a mild office tax people joke about and still buy at the station.
The paired truths—“we don’t really do ochugen anymore” and cakes when invited to dinner—match how households actually talk.
Reciprocity as a trap, PTA debates, café meetups with nothing in hand, and looking up manners pages make taken-for-granted habits visible without invented memoir.
Threshold concentration (arriving, returning, marking a season) is the right everyday map, not “Japanese people are generous.”

issues.location: How Japanese People Experience the Small Bag — “Japanese people often prefer this to a long verbal performance of gratitude”
issues.problem: Slightly mind-reads a national preference; many people are simply following the expected object, not choosing gifts over speeches.
issues.suggestion: Frame as a common pattern: the wrapped item often does the thanks so the talk can stay light—not as a personality preference.

issues.problem: The manners-page correction is locally true; the genetic joke is not how people would describe looking up 香典 or お見舞い.
issues.suggestion: Say the defaults are looked up because ceremonial rules are not everyday knowledge—even for locals.
